title: Ordered map
hints: This is the Module 3 LRU list made generic: a `map[K]*entry[K, V]` finds an entry in O(1), and the `prev`/`next` links keep the order. Every type mention inside the methods needs its parameters: `&entry[K, V]{...}`, `var zero V`.

`Set` on a new key links the entry after `m.tail` (or makes it the `head` of an empty list). `Delete` fixes the neighbours: `e.prev.next = e.next` or, if `e` was first, `m.head = e.next`; same for the other side with `m.tail`.

To survive a delete during ranging, read the link **before** yielding: `for e := m.head; e != nil; { next := e.next; if !yield(e.key, e.value) { return }; e = next }`. `Keys` can range over `m.All()` and yield only `k`; `Collect` is `m := New[K, V](); for k, v := range seq { m.Set(k, v) }`.
